newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast vows to help street children.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast vows to help street children.

text.p: Ivory Coast, in a crackdown on violent crime, said on Friday it would work to solve the problem of 175,000 street children who live, work, beg or steal on the streets of its major towns and cities.

Communication Minister Daniele Boni-Claverie said in a message on state television that a new government initiative sought to help children who were truly alone and ensure that families took proper care of those who lived at home.
"These precarious conditions... expose them to all sorts of danger -- drugs, prostitution, paedophilia, alcohol," she said.
The government has earmarked 300 million CFA francs ($582,000) to help ease the plight of the children, whose numbers have risen from 142,000 in 1991.

The commercial capital Abidjan has an estimated 30,000 street children, who shine shoes, sell fruit and biscuits, and guard parked cars. Ages range from four to 18 years with a majority aged between 10 and 15. The older ones often bully the younger ones or organise them into to gangs of thieves.
A cabinet statement published in the government daily Fraternite Matin on Friday announced proposals to stem the growing tide of street children.
They included creating special projects with non-governmental organisations to take care of children who have no families.
Families whose children roam the streets will be given a month to take proper care of them or face legal action. Police will also set up special squads to deal with the problem. ($1=516 CFA francs)
